numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In the trust-exact trust-region solver, `_minimize_trust_region` constructs the next trust-region subproblem `m_proposed` at every proposed point before deciding whether to accept the step, which evaluates the Hessian early. This wastes Hessian evaluations for rejected steps and can fail/raise an error when a proposed point lies outside the Hessian’s numerical domain. Additionally, if `fun(x_proposed)` returns `nan`, the trust-region comparisons evaluate to `False`, so the solver may stop progressing and terminate only when `iterationlimit` is reached.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Only evaluate `fun` at the proposed point to compute actual reduction (using `actual_reduction = m.fun - fun(x_proposed)`) and treat `nan` trial objective values as `+inf` so the step is rejected and the trust radius shrinks. Create the Hessian-based subproblem at the proposed point only after the step is accepted.
trigger_conditions: When `_minimize_trust_region` is called and a step is proposed (trust-exact solver).
When the proposed point `x_proposed` lies outside the Hessian’s numerical domain so Hessian evaluation/usage can error during `m_proposed = subproblem(x_proposed, fun, jac, hess, hessp)`.
When `fun(x_proposed)` returns `nan`, causing trust-region comparisons to evaluate to `False`, leading to no progress and termination at `iterationlimit`.
oracle_clues: Pre-fix behavior: when a step is proposed, the code created `m_proposed = subproblem(x_proposed, fun, jac, hess, hessp)` before checking acceptance; only `m_proposed.fun` was used later in `actual_reduction = m.fun - m_proposed.fun`.
Pre-fix acceptance computation used `m_proposed.fun`: `actual_reduction = m.fun - m_proposed.fun`.
Post-fix change for numerical handling: compute `proposed_value = fun(x_proposed)` and if `np.isnan(proposed_value)`, set `proposed_value = np.inf`, then `actual_reduction = m.fun - proposed_value`.
Post-fix change for work ordering: create the new subproblem only after accepting the step: `m = subproblem(x, fun, jac, hess, hessp, **subproblem_init_kw)` (after `if rho > eta`).
Issue statement: failure mode includes “may terminate with an error raised” and “run without progress until the iterationlimit is reached (if `fun` returns `nan`).”

provenance.value: In the trust-exact trust-region solver, a Hessian-based subproblem is constructed at each proposed point before deciding whether to accept the step, causing unnecessary Hessian evaluations and failing/terminating when the proposed point lies outside the Hessian’s numerical domain; additionally, if the trial objective fun(x_proposed) returns NaN, the solver can stop progressing (trust-region comparisons evaluate to False) and may run until iterationlimit is reached.

Only evaluate the objective at the proposed point to compute actual reduction; treat NaN trial objective values as +inf so the step is rejected and the trust radius shrinks, and only construct the new Hessian subproblem after the proposed step is accepted.

In the trust-exact trust-region solver, `_minimize_trust_region` constructs the next trust-region subproblem `m_proposed` at every proposed point before deciding whether to accept the step, which evaluates the Hessian early. This wastes Hessian evaluations for rejected steps and can fail/raise an error when a proposed point lies outside the Hessian’s numerical domain. Additionally, if `fun(x_proposed)` returns `nan`, the trust-region comparisons evaluate to `False`, so the solver may stop progressing and terminate only when `iterationlimit` is reached.

Only evaluate `fun` at the proposed point to compute actual reduction (using `actual_reduction = m.fun - fun(x_proposed)`) and treat `nan` trial objective values as `+inf` so the step is rejected and the trust radius shrinks. Create the Hessian-based subproblem at the proposed point only after the step is accepted.
